hero_deck: Follow one portfolio across three versions, from a template I rented to a system I wrote.
hero_rv_txt: I began with templates I could not bend, and ended by building it myself — design, code and the case for the work now sit in one asset I control end to end.
act1_verdict: Qualified on paper, unfamiliar in the room.
act1_lede: Start with the problem: good work nobody can place.
act1_g1_l: I apply for roles whose posts list what a candidate must have. No post lists what a candidate is expected to sound like.
act1_g1_r: Meeting every requirement is what gets an application considered; being understood is what gets it believed, and only the first is ever written down.
act1_g2_l: My own credentials are an MBA, a MicroMasters and a Microsoft specialization. Not one of them showed what I can actually build.
act1_g2_r: Research estimates work sample predicts job performance at about 3× more than education. A running page shows what I did with the diplomas
act1_g3_l: Three in four hiring teams say they receive AI-written applications – turning openings into odysseys for qualified candidates.
act1_g3_r: 65% of hiring managers say skills are harder to verify as anybody can generate a fluent claim in seconds. Every figure here is backed up in public commit history.
act1_g4_l: Employment in Lima, Peru has grown 22% since 2019, while the share of it held by workers under 25 has fallen by about a third.
act1_g4_r: Instead of contracting, local market is moving toward work that cannot be automated. That is the direction this website is built toward.
act1_foot: Sources: Sackett et al. (2022) on selection validity; Robert Half, November 2025, n = 2,000+; Deel Global Hiring Report 2026; INEI Encuesta Permanente de Empleo Nacional, May–July 2026.
act2_lede: Four stops, from designing pictures of software to building it.
act2_verdict: I learned to build — then made building answer to a standard I wrote down.
act2_s1_x: I designed for years in Canva, Figma, and Framer while builders like Webflow, Wix, and WordPress stayed someone else's system.
act2_s2_x: I chose to learn front-end development itself, not coding in the abstract, with a Microsoft specialization laying the foundations.
act2_s3_x: The first portfolio wasn't a portfolio. It was jdigital.pe, a brand site — re-pointed once I knew what I actually had to show.
act2_s4_x: Eight pages replaced the scroll. Each case got its own route, and the architecture became part of what the work shows.
act3_verdict: Two architectures, one standard. The differences are decisions, not accidents.
act3_lede: Some decisions carried across both builds. Others belong to one. Filter to see which.
act3_c1_x: No framework, no build step, no dependency I cannot read end to end.
act3_c1_rv_txt: Nothing to migrate when a major version lands. No security-patch treadmill. A payload small enough to stay fast on a mid-range phone over Peruvian mobile data — which is what most recruiters will use to open it.
act3_c2_x: WCAG AA held as a build gate, usable with screen readers and keyboards.
act3_c2_rv_txt1: Every meaningful image carries alt text, every control is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus state, and contrast is verified in both themes rather than assumed.
act3_c2_rv_txt2: Layout resolves at three declared breakpoints — 767px and below, 768 to 1023, and 1024 up. Those are the three the stylesheets actually declare, not a convention borrowed from a framework.
act3_c3_x: Ten sections, one type scale, Flexbox and Grid throughout.
act3_c3_rv_txt1: The ontology: ten reusable organisms, each owning one job — navigation, hero, work cards, capability carousel, contact.
act3_c3_rv_txt2: The taxonomy: design rules declared once at the root as custom properties, inherited everywhere, overridden nowhere.
act3_c3_rv_txt3: The choreography: one scroll, one order, every visitor served the same sequence whether or not it was the one they came for.
act3_c4_x: Speed came from AI; the standard stayed with me. Workflows orchestrated with Claude and Claude Code, early 2026.
act3_c4_rv_txt1: Structured XML dispatches govern every build session — scope, constraints, and approval gates written before execution. Claude Code executes with Plan Mode previews reviewed before code lands; deployment follows hard rules with named commit intent — register, direct push, or a pull request with its link for manual approval — and authorship is logged to a single human author.
act3_c5_x: The same type scale and token layer, now carried across a shared page chassis.
act3_c5_rv_txt: Each case gets its own route, its own dictionary and its own entry point, so a recruiter can be sent to one page rather than to a scroll position. The cost is a chassis that must stay identical across eight pages — and one defect in it is eight defects.
act3_c6_x: The second build runs against a signed, enumerated scope with exit conditions.
act3_c6_rv_btn: HOW THE SECOND BUILD IS GOVERNED
act3_c6_rv_txt: Every stage is dispatched as a written prompt with preflight checks, approval gates and a completion report. Improvements that fall outside the list are logged in one line and not built. The discipline is the deliverable as much as the site is.
act4_verdict: Two builds, one measure each. The gap is the point.
act4_insight: Thirty-two active build-days on the single page. Seventeen on the multi-page, after finishing the Microsoft Front-End certificate. Same person, roughly half the days.
dash_r1: The signal isn't the volume. It's the ratio. 286 commits mean momentum; 52 pull requests mean the momentum was reviewed.
dash_r2: Beneath the numbers sits a qualitative floor: the build meets a graded professional rubric for semantic structure, accessibility, styling discipline, interactivity, and responsive behavior.
dash_r3: What transfers to your team isn't my code. It's this operating habit.
dash_foot: Method: public commit history of github.com/jdsaire/jdigital and github.com/jdsaire/legacy-desops, summed across both, 24 Apr – 06 Jul 2026 (73 days). Rates are simple averages — 286÷73, 52÷10.4, 286÷52.
dash2_r1: Half the days, and a defect inventory instead of a fresh start. The second build spends its time differently: less authoring, more governing.
dash2_foot: Method: public commit history of github.com/jdsaire/designops, 10 Jul – 08 Sep 2026. Anything dated after 06 Sep is forecast and badged as such.
act5_verdict: What worked, what didn't, what I'd keep.
act5_intro: The story reads clean in hindsight. It wasn't. Here is each build, honestly.
act5_h2_b2: One bug outlasted my main environment.
act5_h3_b2: Skills that carry intent between sessions.
act5_h3_b3: A written scope that can say no.
act5_sequel: The sequel is already dispatched: the Spanish layer, the closing audit, and a second brief series before 2026 ends.
act5_m1_b1: Moved organisms before deciding where they belonged.
act5_m1_b2: Two sections became stubs; one stayed too heavy.
act5_m1_b3: Allocation, not architecture, was the mistake.
act5_m2_b1: Eight pages share one navigation layer.
act5_m2_b2: Two missing tokens broke it on four of them.
act5_m2_b3: Static checks passed; the browser didn't.
act5_m3_b1: An enumerated scope with exit conditions.
act5_m3_b2: Improvements logged in one line, not argued.
act5_m3_b3: The project can end, which it previously could not.
act5_m_sequel: The sequel: applications sent, and the parking lot read once — after the fifth one.
convert_c1_x: A media-accreditation platform with a full UX dossier and 545 tests behind it.
convert_c2_x: A payment-verification flow rebuilt as an operator-legible sequence.
sch_verdict: Seventy-three days on the first build. Seventeen on the second.
sch_lede: Each epic below is reconstructed from the public commit history of both single-page repositories. Planned-capacity days appear here and nowhere else on this page.
sch_note: Reconstructed from the public commit history of github.com/jdsaire/jdigital and github.com/jdsaire/legacy-desops, summed across both — 24 Apr – 06 Jul 2026. 32 active build-days; three further dates in June carried document uploads rather than site code and are excluded. The closing Ground Zero reorganization (06 Jul, ~1 day) is my own account, not a commit. No task appears that the record cannot support.
gantt_seq_text: Sequence: the jdigital repository ran first, then legacy-desops, then designops. This is the order the three repositories were worked in, not a chain of blocking dependencies.
gantt_noscript: This component renders from its data object and requires JavaScript. Every window it draws is also stated in the note below.
gantt_caption_body: Bars are calendar spans, not effort. A gap is a real gap: nothing was committed on those days. Each row carries an information button naming that row's window and where it came from. The dotted row is my own account rather than a commit. The record ends on 06 September 2026 and nothing is drawn past it — four further stages are dispatched and carry no date to draw: this one, the Spanish layer, the repository README and the closing audit.
